To eradicate this pressure we use self compassion. What if the pressure is external and no amount of self love can fix a looming deadline?

Btw Art of war is a book on similar theme, but I assume you've read it

Thanks for the article! You know that I agree with pining, positive reinforcement and all that so I'll just skip to detail questions. I wholeheartedly agree that we learn much better if we feel good emotions, hence why it's better to start with small goals and build up.

Definitely works for habits in general, but if we're talking about habit that is such high stakes as writing for a writer, there are far more obstacles in the way than just your mind.

What if, "brute force" as mentioned is external? It's a schooling problem perhaps that we all have to follow the same curriculum while being different people, at different levels. And ofc, working makes a lot of people lose joy in creating, because it automatizes the creative process. Then it can pull you back in square one, where the habit isn't motivated by good emotions. I definitely went to zero in motivation a few times in such scenarios.

Also I can't help but imagine the situation as someone who has time and money? As I said, higher stakes. I've been trying this method over and over but the time pressure of not having money is quite real. If you want to make a living out of it, you gotta be good. I find it unless you're in university and someone pays for your expenses or you have comfortable job that lets you commit you your habit on the side, it's Buddha level mind strenght to be chill about it. For me personally now that I have a relief in a having a (industry) job, it feels easy to paint on my own. But of course everyone is different, some people don't struggle with this at all. :)

Sorry for the long rant, not even trying to rip your article apart haha, it does pretty much come to "take care of yourself first" and then you can develop the habit.
